title: Signed scalar-free chart evaluation in the native internal module category
statement:
Let $S$ be any scheme with its small pro-étale site [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring, put $R_S=p_S^*\Lambda$, and use its internal module category and ordinary uncompleted derived tensor/internal Hom [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. Let $A$ be a commutative ring with a map from the constant ring sheaf $A_S$ to $R_S$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let $P$ be a bounded cochain complex of finite free $A$-modules and put $T^i=R_S\otimes_{A_S}(P^i)_S$ termwise. Here scalar extension is the ordinary relative tensor [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. Let $E_S$ be the section-action equivalence to modules over the section-ring sheaf $B_S$ [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence].

Set $D_P^b=\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^{-b},A)$ with differential $d\phi=(-1)^{b+1}\phi d_P$, and put $D_T=R_S\otimes_{A_S}(D_P)_S$ termwise. For every unbounded complex $F$ of internal $R_S$-modules there is a natural chain isomorphism
$$E_S\operatorname{Tot}(F\otimes_{R_S}D_T)\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_{B_S}^\bullet(E_ST,E_SF).$$
Use the direct-sum total differential and Hom differential of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves, def-pur-hom-complex]. Under the scalar finite-free identifications, its component from $F^a\otimes D_T^b$ is zero on $T^i$ for $i\ne-b$, and for $i=-b$ sends $y\otimes\phi$ to $(x\mapsto y\phi(x))$. For a basis $(e_j)$ of $P^i$, the inverse coordinate is $f\mapsto\sum_j f(e_j)\otimes e_j^*$. The comparison is independent of bases and compatible with slice restriction.

The native complex $D_T$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], and the Hom complex on the right sends every K-injective augmentation of $E_SF$ to a quasi-isomorphism. After localization, the displayed chain map identifies $D_T$ with the native $R\mathcal Hom_{R_S}(T,R_S)$ and is exactly the native evaluation transpose
$$F\otimes_{R_S}^{\mathbf L}R\mathcal Hom_{R_S}(T,R_S)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{R_S}(T,F).$$
The assertion concerns the native tensor and its actual closed adjunction, not an arbitrarily chosen monoidal structure on an equivalent derived category. No flatness of $R_S$ over $A_S$ and no boundedness of $F$ is assumed.

proof.text: Use the ordinary finite-free chain theorem to obtain kappa, epsilon, its normalization, naturality and the inverse in every basis.

Realize a chosen finite scalar basis. The rank-one constant module is the constant ring, and extension sends it to the coefficient unit. Additivity preserves finite products, giving an isomorphism of every realized term to a finite free sheaf. Apply finite-retract dual exactness to its inverse pair. The realized complex has the original finite bounds. Bounded exact-term Hom therefore sends every quasi-isomorphism to a quasi-isomorphism.

For an acyclic native Z, the section Z is acyclic. Apply the preceding Hom invariance to 0→section Z. Ordinary Hom is additive, so Hom(T,0) is zero and Hom(T,section Z) is acyclic. Transport through epsilon Z and reflect exactness through the faithful section equivalence. This proves the native acyclic tensor test. The quasi-isomorphism assertion for every K-injective augmentation follows directly from Hom invariance.

Take the evaluation-normalized comparison data S,M,t,theta from moduleObject_ringedSite_derived_comparison. Apply generic ordinary evaluation localization with these fixed data, kappa, epsilon, its formula and naturality, the proved acyclic tensor test and full Hom invariance. The fixed K-injective augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism, so Hom invariance makes the ordinary-to-derived Hom comparison invertible. Every factor on the right of the localization equation is now invertible. The left derived Hom comparison is also invertible. Cancel it, reflect isomorphisms through the derived section equivalence, and cancel tensor with the dual isomorphism delta. This proves the native evaluation transpose is invertible. Assemble all ordinary and derived clauses.
